Interface Body

All Known Implementing Classes:
Body.Bytes, Body.Input, Body.Output
public sealed interface Body permits Body.Bytes, Body.Input, Body.Output
A message body: bytes in memory, a blocking InputStream (how a backend hands over a request body), or a Body.Writer that writes straight to the connection (a streamed response). Blocking is fine: each request runs on its own virtual thread.

Two kinds of writer, by what a flush means:

  • Body.writer: the body is sent when the writer returns. Its flushes are ignored, so an encoder that flushes when it finishes (forj-codec's Json.encode(value, out) does) doesn't cost anything: a small body still goes out in one write with a Content-Length, and a large one streams as the server's buffer fills, so memory stays bounded either way.
  • Body.streaming: each flush() sends what's written so far, before the writer returns. For server-sent events, streamed tokens, progress reports. It changes when the client sees the bytes, not how much memory is used.

A streamed body (Body.Input) can be read once. Reading methods throw UncheckedIOException when the underlying stream fails.

      static Body writer(Body.Writer writer, long length)
      A body written to the connection when the response is sent; length is -1 when unknown. The writer's flushes are ignored: everything is sent once it returns (or as the server's buffer fills). For early sends, use streaming(Writer).

    • streaming

      static Body streaming(Body.Writer writer)
      A body whose writer sends what it has written each time it calls flush(): server-sent events, streamed tokens, progress. Its length is unknown, so it's sent chunked.
